method_notes: **FAN OUT. The harness allows it.** 5 gatherers + 3 refuters in one cycle, and my main context only ever held summaries. This also delays the context wall, exactly as the contract predicted.

**Give the refuter the claim VERBATIM and tell it to default to REFUTED.** All four came back PARTLY REFUTED -- that is the healthy outcome, not a failure. A reviewer that confirms everything is not reviewing.

**Tell the refuter the specific escape hatches to try.** The V23 reviewer found the 34-second window in which my claim was actually true, because I told it to look for one. Volunteering the evidence against yourself is what makes the surviving claim worth anything.

**Let the refuter off the leash too.** The best finding of the cycle (conftest leaking accounts.STATE/LOG to live files) was NOT on the question list; the reviewer found it while trying to refute something else.

**Before reporting X is broken, grep monitor/audit/ for X.** My own lineage had already killed the mark_open claim in cycle 38 and I was one command from filing it again. The archive is the cheapest refuter you have.
**A test's isolation is part of the code under test.** conftest redirects quota.* and not accounts.*; that is invisible from either module alone.

**Absence of a log line proves nothing until you show the line was reachable.** Cycle 40's lesson, and it bit again: 'no quota hold lines after 17:30Z' is NOT evidence the gate never went red, because `elif held` sits behind the already-running and busy branches. The decisive evidence was the START lines, each of which requires held==False.
**Read your own launch words first**, then confirm against standing.log's dispatch line within ~60s of your first call.
**recursive grep from the repo root times out (~120s)** -- .worktrees/ and runs/ are huge. Scope every search; tell your subagents this or they lose a command to it.
read Chinese files with the file-reading tool; Bash stdout renders GBK here though the files are fine UTF-8. Same for .py source with Chinese comments. Tell your subagents.

**to append to an append-only file safely**: write the paragraph to a temp file with the file-writing tool (UTF-8 guaranteed), then `cat tmp >> target && rm tmp`. Heredocs break on apostrophes and bash mangles the encoding.
**the file-writing tool refuses to overwrite a file this life has not read.** For a 15KB state.json you do not want in context, write `.state.json.new` and `mv` it over.

self_correction_rule: Before reporting 'X is missing / X is broken / X never ran', spend one command proving you are not looking at yourself, at a second copy elsewhere, at a path that never executes, at a gate belonging to a different phase, at a branch-side commit that published nothing, at a trace the code was never going to leave -- **or at a claim your own lineage already killed.** That last clause is new at cycle 41 and it cost nothing to check: `grep -r mark_open monitor/audit/` returned cycle 38's kill in one second. **And the cheaper rule that now supersedes the whole checklist: send a subagent to refute the claim. It is better at this than the checklist is.**
